military.study_title: An army trying to get home

sections.title: Withdrawal becomes a race against time
sections.text: Read the operational sequence through the Romanian ultimatum, the Hungarian transit instructions and the struggle to provision the departing army.
cases: The ultimatum reaches the evening report
Arad: provisions for 80,000 men and 30,000 animals

sections.title: What had to move with the troops
sections.text: Railways, food, hospitals and animals give the withdrawal its material scale. These records turn an order to leave into a set of practical transport problems.

sections.title: The limits of military authority
sections.text: Read the appeal against internment beside the later internment traffic and the reports of unrest. The case pages distinguish the orders, reports and outcomes each telegram actually records.
cases: Kiev unrest and soldiers’ council neutrality

naval.study_title: The Black Sea network runs in reverse

sections.title: Cargo and the changing purpose of ships
sections.text: The same shipping network carries supplies, commercial cargo and people trying to leave. Begin with the Black Sea shipping messages and the Poti loading instruction.

sections.title: Sale, seizure and control
sections.text: Ship-sale terms reveal who could authorize a sale, how payment was to work and which rights the German side wanted to retain.

sections.title: Cash that an army could use
sections.text: A request for money becomes more revealing when it specifies the currency, the route and the denomination. Follow the crown shortage from the airlift request to the later complete banknote instruction.
cases: A million crowns a day by aircraft

sections.title: Contracts and assets at the end of occupation
sections.text: Purchasing orders, resale permissions and abandoned transport connect military withdrawal with a commercial world that still expected accounts to be settled.
cases: Silk resale recovered from two receptions

sections.title: Pay, exchange and administration
sections.text: Allowances and exchange rates show the continuing administrative demands behind the larger movements.

sections.title: Keeping a shrinking network connected
sections.text: Schedules, broken links and relay instructions show the communications system under strain. A request to repeat a message is also evidence of what its first reception failed to preserve.

sections.title: Keys, procedure and changing authority
sections.text: Read key-reuse instructions beside command traffic: the network had to remain intelligible while its political and military surroundings changed.

sections.title: People behind the call signs
sections.text: A delayed departure, a supper query and the Seifert correspondence preserve the human scale of the wireless service.

sections.title: Permission to leave, permission to stay
sections.text: The end of the war appears here as a personal administrative problem: who may travel, who can be discharged and who may remain where they live.
cases: Kremp asks for a departure date

sections.title: An organization still moving its people
sections.text: Appointments and transfers continue beside the withdrawal. Read them as evidence of the institutions and destinations named in the messages, without supplying identities the ciphertext cannot establish.
cases: A medical return to the unit

caucasus.study_title: The Black Sea network runs in reverse

sections.title: The mission before the withdrawal
sections.text: October correspondence follows staffing, equipment and procurement around Tiflis. It provides the institutional background for the later evacuation traffic.

sections.title: Representation, cargo and departure
sections.text: The Polish appointment, Poti traffic and later armistice material bring diplomatic representation and material withdrawal into the same regional frame.
cases: The damaged first part of the Poti message
An armistice notice across two receptions
